---
title: "Frequently asked questions"
---

## Projects

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Is there a project in the course?

Not a separate one. Each assignment has a project-like question instead, so that:

- everyone works on similar problems;
- we can give better guidance and support;
- you learn the ideas by applying them.

There is no separate final project.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What does a project question look like?

An example, an activity classifier:

1. Build a classifier for activities such as walking and running.
2. Start with a public dataset.
3. Collect your own data with a smartphone.
4. Train and evaluate a classifier on your own data.
5. Optional: deploy the classifier on your phone.
:::

## Prerequisites

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What are the prerequisites?

There are no formal prerequisites, but you should know:

- Python programming (ES 242 or equivalent)
- data structures and algorithms
- probability and statistics
- linear algebra
- basic calculus
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What is the prerequisite exam?

A required exam that checks you have the background to do well in the course.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How do I prepare for the prerequisite exam?

- Review your undergraduate course material.
- Work through the [preparation material](index.qmd#prerequisites) on the home page.
- Focus on Python, linear algebra and probability.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## What if I do not clear the prerequisite exam?

You will not be allowed to enrol in the course. The instructor sets the cutoff score, which is not announced
beforehand.
:::

## Classroom

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Can I use my laptop in class?

No. Laptops are not allowed in class, for any reason.
:::

## Quizzes

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What if I miss a quiz?

- The quiz scores 0%.
- The "best 3 of 4" rule covers a missed quiz.
- There are no makeup quizzes, for any reason.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Are quizzes open book?

No. All quizzes and exams are closed book, with no notes.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## When do I get my answer sheets back?

4 to 5 working days after the quiz.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What is the quiz schedule and format?

- 2 quizzes in the mid-semester period and 2 in the end-semester period.
- A mix of multiple-choice and written questions.
:::

## Assignments

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## What if I miss an assignment deadline?

No extensions are given, for any reason.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Where do I ask questions about an assignment?

1. First, on the Slack channel **#assignments**.
2. If there is no answer within 2 days, email the instructor.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Can I use a language other than Python?

No. All assignments must be in Python.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How are assignments evaluated?

Each assignment ends with a viva:

1. TAs compare the submitted code with the code you run live.
2. No changes are allowed during the viva (you will get a warning).
3. You demonstrate the code and answer questions.

| Assignment marks | Share |
|:--|--:|
| Code functionality | 50% |
| Understanding of the assignment | 25% |
| Code quality | 12.5% |
| Theory | 12.5% |

Viva questions are 75% about the assignment and 25% about theory.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Are assignments individual or group work?

Group work. Everyone in a team gets the same grade.
:::

## Attendance

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What is the attendance policy?

See the [attendance policy](grading.qmd#attendance-6) on the grading page.
:::

## Auditing

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Can I audit the course?

You are welcome to attend all lectures. Auditors cannot:

- have assignments graded (TA time is limited);
- join an assignment team formally;
- get official course credit.
:::

## Computing

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What computing resources are available?

Google Cloud credits are usually provided for the course. They are enough for all assignments; we post an update
with setup instructions when the credits are available.
:::
